# requireNonNull

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not `null` or `undefined`.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonNull() — Returns the value after checking that it is not `null` or `undefined`. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonNull<T>(value?: T | null | undefined, message?: string): T;
```

The absent values, and only those: `0`, `""` and `false` are present values and do not qualify.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter              | Type                     | Description                                                   |
| :--------------------- | :----------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value` _(optional)_   | `T \| null \| undefined` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ | `string`                 | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with `null` or `undefined` excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception              | Condition                           |
| :--------------------- | :---------------------------------- |
| `NullPointerException` | the value is `null` or `undefined`. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonNull(0); // => 0
requireNonNull(""); // => ""
requireNonNull(null); // throws NullPointerException
requireNonNull(undefined); // throws NullPointerException
```
